_comment: What a condition's operator reads as where it sits, and whether that place takes it: core/condition_eval.py written_operator and condition_issues, and the Programmer's writtenOperator and takesOperator (api/conditionEval.ts), which its pickers and the trigger summaries read. Run by tests/test_condition_written_operator.py and conditionEval.test.ts. A case with no 'operator' is one saved without it; 'written' null is an explicit null kept as written.

cases.name: a State Change trigger saved with no operator fires on any change
a State Change trigger's null operator fires on any change
a State Change trigger's blank operator fires on any change
a State Change trigger's any is itself
any in capitals is no operator
a space is no operator, and not blank
a State Change trigger takes an alias as written
a State Change trigger takes an operator's own name
a Skip If saved with no operator reads as eq
a Skip If's blank operator is no operator
a Skip If's null operator is no operator
a Conditional takes an alias as written
a Wait Until takes an alias as written
a guard does not take any
a guard takes an alias as written
a word nobody knows is kept as written and not taken
an operator in another case is no operator
